result.summary: Full S1-S14 pass over REQ-022 (withdraw from a registration and free the seat: decideWithdrawOutcome/withdrawRegistration/getRegistrationForEventAndUser in domain/registration.ts, the targeted registerForEvent row-reuse change, new handlers/withdraw.ts with a two-step confirm/cancel callback UX), branch feature/WF02-REQ-022, commit 1b185d1. Read core-directives.md and security-invariants.md in full, docs/agents/design/REQ-022.md in full, then read apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts and apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts myself end to end (not REVIEWER's summary) and traced every call path by hand. S7 (PRIMARY FOCUS, task step 3) -- PASS. Read registerForEvent's modification directly: the transaction/lock structure is unchanged (still `for('update')` on the events row, first and only capacity-serializing lock in the function), decideRegistrationOutcome is byte-for-byte identical to REQ-020 (confirmed by reading it -- zero lines differ), and the only change is (a) the existing-row SELECT now also projects `id`, (b) a withdrawn row's admission is normalized to null purely as the value fed into decideRegistrationOutcome (the function itself never sees the raw 'withdrawn' string), and (c) step 8 branches UPDATE-vs-INSERT on whether a withdrawn row was found, naming only admission/source/qr_token in the UPDATE's SET clause (id/created_at untouched, confirmed by reading the statement -- no column list surprises). This is genuinely surgical, not a rewrite. Independently verified the withdraw-lock/register-lock non-contention claim rather than taking it on trust. withdrawRegistration's only lock is `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the target registrations row by id (registration.ts:357-367) -- it never touches the events table, never opens a transaction that reads/locks events, and never computes or writes anything capacity-related; it flips exactly one column (admission) on one already-identified row. Traced what would break this: capacity correctness depends on registerForEvent always computing seatsLeft via a fresh COUNT(admission='admitted') taken inside the same transaction as its events-row lock (registration.ts:157-161) -- never a cached/stored counter. Because withdrawRegistration performs no capacity bookkeeping of its own (no counter increment/decrement, no seatsLeft field written anywhere), there is no shared mutable state for its registrations-row lock to race against register's events-row lock; the two transactions are read-committed-consistent with each other regardless of interleaving. Constructed the counterfactual explicitly, per task step 3: had this design instead cached a seats-left counter or required withdraw to decrement any capacity-adjacent value, withdraw's registrations-only lock WOULD have been insufficient (a lost-update window would open) -- but the actual code contains no such counter anywhere; computeSeatsLeft (event.ts, REQ-017, unmodified) still does a live COUNT every time. Ran registerForEvent's own concurrency test myself: `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts -t 'atomic capacity'` -> 1/1 passed against real Postgres (exactly one of two concurrent last-seat registrations admitted). Did not repeat REVIEWER's additional 50-iteration/20-iteration withdraw-vs-register stress scenarios -- REVIEWER's own report names the specific mechanism (registrations-only lock never contends with the events lock) that my independent trace above reaches the same conclusion about from the code itself, so this is corroboration from two independent readings, not reliance on REVIEWER's say-so. Authorization / forged-callback check (task steps 5-6, the new surface not present in REQ-020/021) -- PASS, and this is the central new risk this diff introduces. Traced getRegistrationForEventAndUser (registration.ts:412-436): scoped by `(event_id, user_id)` where user_id is always the caller's own resolveActingUser(...).id (handlers/withdraw.ts:57, 64-67) -- never an id supplied by the caller -- so the /withdraw command's own display path cannot be tricked into showing or acting on someone else's registration. The higher-risk surface is the callback: `withdraw:confirm:` carries a bare registration id as callback_data, which is fully attacker/forgeable (any Telegram client can send an arbitrary callbackQuery with fabricated data to a bot it can message). Traced the confirm handler (handlers/withdraw.ts:101-154): it resolves actingUser from ctx.from.id (server-side, not client-suppliable) and passes both registrationId (attacker-suppliable) and actingUser.id (server-derived) into withdrawRegistration. Inside withdrawRegistration (registration.ts:348-401), the row is fetched FRESH by registrationId alone under FOR UPDATE (step 1), and decideWithdrawOutcome's row 2 (registration.ts:334) compares that freshly-read row's actual `userId` column against the actingUserId parameter -- if they differ, the function returns `{kind:'not-owner'}` at line 334-336 BEFORE reaching the write at line 387. Constructed the negative case directly: crafted the scenario of user A forging `withdraw:confirm:` -- resolveActingUser resolves A's own tgId to A's own users.id regardless of what registrationId A supplies, the row lookup returns B's row (userId=B), ownerUserId(B) !== actingUserId(A) fires the not-owner branch, zero write occurs (registration.ts:382-384 returns before the UPDATE), and the confirm callback handler maps 'not-owner' to the SAME generic refusedNotFound string used for a genuinely nonexistent registration (handlers/withdraw.ts:138-142) -- no disclosure that the id belonged to a real, different user's registration. This closes the forged-callback authorization surface: the callback_data id is untrusted input, but the write path never trusts it for anything except which row to lock and re-derive ownership from -- authorization is enforced against the DB-read owner, not the callback payload or any earlier display-time state. TOCTOU re-verification (task step 7) -- PASS, independently re-confirmed (not taken from REVIEWER's report). withdrawRegistration's SELECT...FOR UPDATE (registration.ts:357-367) is a fresh read inside its own transaction, executed at confirm time; the checkedInAt value used by decideWithdrawOutcome (line 377) comes from THIS read, not from getRegistrationForEventAndUser's earlier display-only read (which populates only the /withdraw command's prompt, handlers/withdraw.ts:57, and is never passed into or reused by the confirm callback -- the confirm handler re-derives everything from registrationId + a fresh DB call). Traced the code path end to end: no variable carries a checkedInAt/admission value from the display step across the callback boundary; callback_data carries only the opaque registrationId. The race (checked in during the confirm-prompt window) is structurally closed. History-not-editable / S6-adjacent (task step 8) -- PASS. decideWithdrawOutcome checks `checkedInAt !== null` (row 3, line 337-339) BEFORE the eligibility check (row 4), so a checked-in registration is refused as 'checked-in' regardless of its admission value, and this check is inside the same authoritative, lock-taking function used by the only write path (withdrawRegistration) -- there is no second withdraw-capable code path. Confirmed handlers/checkin.ts and domain/checkin.ts are untouched by this diff (`git diff master...feature/WF02-REQ-022 -- apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.ts apps/bot/src/domain/checkin.ts` -> empty), so no alternate handler exists that could either withdraw a checked-in registration or set checked_in_at on a withdrawn one. The DB-level CHECK constraint `chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted` (cited in the design, pre-existing, unmodified) is a second independent backstop. S8 (task step 4) -- PASS. withdrawRegistration contains exactly one writeAuditLog call (registration.ts:390-397), reached only on the single 'withdrawn'-outcome branch, inside the same transaction as the one-column UPDATE, after the early return at line 382-384 for every other outcome kind (not-found/not-owner/checked-in/not-eligible) which returns with zero write and zero audit call. Confirmed by reading the function body directly -- no loop, no retry wrapper, no second call site for writeAuditLog with action 'registration.withdraw' anywhere in the diff (grepped both changed files). S1 -- N/A, reason: no new personal data is stored or consent-checked; this diff only ever flips an existing registration row's admission column and reads pre-existing columns (id/eventId/userId/admission/checkedInAt), none of which are Profile/consent fields. S2 -- PASS (see authorization/forged-callback finding above) -- withdrawal has no role/organizer/EventStaff dimension by design (any member withdraws only their own registration), and the negative case (acting on someone else's registration) is proven refused above. S3 -- PASS. Neither getRegistrationForEventAndUser, decideWithdrawOutcome, nor withdrawRegistration ever reads or returns a PII column (name/phone/email/employer) -- both SELECTs project only id/eventId/userId/admission/checkedInAt (registration.ts:357-364, 417-424). No list/export/broadcast surface is touched by this diff. S4 -- N/A, no qr_token/InviteCode generation or validation touched; qrToken is passed through unchanged in the register row-reuse UPDATE (same value computation as before, only the write target changed from INSERT to UPDATE). S5/S6 -- N/A for check-in code itself (untouched); the checked-in refusal is covered under 'history-not-editable' above. S9/S10 -- N/A, no notification/scheduler/broadcast code touched by this diff. S11 -- PASS. Grepped both changed domain/handler files for console/log calls -- zero matches. The audit payload for registration.withdraw contains only `{ eventId }` (registration.ts:395), no phone/email/name. The generic non-disclosure refusal (refusedNotFound reused for not-owner) additionally prevents any PII/existence leak through reply text. S12 -- N/A, no export code touched. S13 (migration sign-off, named duty) -- N/A, no migration in this diff. Confirmed via `git diff master...feature/WF02-REQ-022 --stat` (no drizzle .sql file) and a glob for apps/bot/src/db/migrations/** (no results) -- matches the design's explicit 'no schema change' claim (REQ-022.md §0), independently verified against db/schema.ts's existing admission enum/checked_in_at column/unique index rather than trusted from the design doc's assertion alone. S14 -- N/A, no publication/speaker code touched. Commands run myself, real output: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only, outside apps/bot, unchanged by this diff). `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces (apps/web next build, apps/bot tsc) clean. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, full suite) -> 17 files / 196 passed, 0 failures. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts -t 'atomic capacity'` -> 1/1 passed against real Postgres, independently re-run (not reused from REVIEWER's report). One coverage observation (not a gate failure -- the code itself is correct by direct trace above, and this gate verifies the code, not test coverage, which is TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's step): no integration-level test currently exercises withdrawRegistration or the withdraw:confirm handler with a registrationId belonging to a DIFFERENT user's registration (the forged-callback scenario) -- only a pure decideWithdrawOutcome unit test covers 'not-owner' (registration.db.test.ts:555-564). Flagging this as a MINOR issue for TEST-DESIGNER to add an explicit forged-callback/cross-user regression test at Step 3, since this is the single highest-risk new surface this requirement introduces and it currently has no test at the level where a future regression (e.g. someone refactoring the ownership check) would actually be caught. No S1-S14 violation found. All applicable items PASS; N/A items stated with reasons above, none silently skipped.

evidence.forged_callback_finding: A forged withdraw:confirm:<registrationId> callback naming another user's registration CANNOT withdraw it. withdrawRegistration re-reads the target row fresh under FOR UPDATE by id alone, and decideWithdrawOutcome compares that row's actual userId column against the server-resolved actingUserId (never the callback payload) -- a mismatch returns {kind:'not-owner'} before any write, and the handler maps it to the same generic refusedNotFound string used for a nonexistent registration, disclosing nothing.

issues.title: No integration-level regression test for the withdraw forged-callback / cross-user ownership check
issues.description: withdrawRegistration's not-owner path (the highest-risk new authorization surface in REQ-022) is covered only by a pure decideWithdrawOutcome unit test (registration.db.test.ts:555-564). No test drives withdrawRegistration or the withdraw:confirm handler end-to-end with a registrationId belonging to a different user's real row against real Postgres. Code is verified correct by direct trace in this handoff; recommend TEST-DESIGNER add this case at Step 3 so a future regression would be caught.
